sentences.en: Three leaders in their fields answer questions about our relationships with robots
sentences.zh: 三位各自领域的领军人物回答了有关人类与机器人关系的问题。

sentences.en: When asked ‘Should robots be used to colonise other planets?’, cosmology and astrophysics Professor Martin Rees said he believed the solar system would be mapped by robotic craft by the end of the century.
sentences.zh: 有人问：“应当利用机器人去其他行星建立殖民地吗？”宇宙学与天体物理学教授马丁·里斯说，他相信到本世纪末，机器人航天器将完成对太阳系的测绘。

sentences.en: ‘The next step would be mining of asteroids, enabling fabrication of large structures in space without having to bring all the raw materials from Earth. … I think this is more realistic and benign than the … “terraforming”* of planets.’
sentences.zh: “下一步将是开采小行星，这样就能在太空制造大型结构，而不必把所有原材料都从地球运过去。……我认为，比起……把行星‘地球化’，这种做法更现实，也更温和。”

sentences.en: He maintains that colonised planets ‘should be preserved with a status that is analogous to Antarctica here on Earth.’
sentences.zh: 他主张，对已建立殖民地的行星，“应当加以保护，并赋予它们与地球上南极洲相似的地位”。

sentences.en: On the question of using robots to colonise other planets and exploit mineral resources, engineering Professor Daniel Wolpert replied, ‘I don’t see a pressing need to colonise other planets unless we can bring [these] resources back to Earth.
sentences.zh: 谈到利用机器人在其他行星建立殖民地、开发矿产资源时，工程学教授丹尼尔·沃尔珀特回答：“除非我们能把［这些］资源带回地球，否则我看不出在其他行星建立殖民地有多迫切。

sentences.en: The vast majority of Earth is currently inaccessible to us.
sentences.zh: 目前，地球的绝大部分地方我们都还无法进入。

sentences.en: Using robots to gather resources nearer to home would seem to be a better use of our robotic tools.’
sentences.zh: 利用机器人在离我们更近的地方搜集资源，似乎更能发挥这些机器人工具的作用。”

sentences.en: Meanwhile, for anthropology Professor Kathleen Richardson, the idea of ‘colonisation’ of other planets seemed morally dubious: ‘I think whether we do something on Earth or on Mars we should always do it in the spirit of a genuine interest in “the Other”, not to impose a particular model, but to meet “the Other”.’
sentences.zh: 与此同时，人类学教授凯瑟琳·理查森认为，到其他行星进行“殖民”的想法在道德上值得怀疑：“我认为，无论我们是在地球上还是在火星上做事，都应该出于对‘他者’真诚的兴趣，目的是与‘他者’相遇，而非把某一种模式强加给对方。”

sentences.en: In response to the second question, ‘How soon will machine intelligence outstrip human intelligence?’, Rees mentions robots that are advanced enough to beat humans at chess, but then goes on to say, ‘Robots are still limited in their ability to sense their environment: they can’t yet recognise and move the pieces on a real chessboard as cleverly as a child can.
sentences.zh: 对于第二个问题“机器智能还有多久会超过人类智能？”，里斯提到，如今已有机器人先进到能够在国际象棋上击败人类。但他接着说：“机器人感知环境的能力仍然有限；它们还不能像孩子那样灵巧地识别并移动真实棋盘上的棋子。

sentences.en: Later this century, however, their more advanced successors may relate to their surroundings, and to people, as adeptly as we do.
sentences.zh: 不过，到本世纪后期，更先进的新一代机器人与环境和人打交道时，或许会像我们一样得心应手。

sentences.en: Moral questions then arise. … Should we feel guilty about exploiting [sophisticated robots]?
sentences.zh: 那时，道德问题就会随之出现。……我们应当因为利用［先进的机器人］而感到内疚吗？

sentences.en: Should we fret if they are underemployed, frustrated, or bored?’
sentences.zh: 如果它们没有充分发挥作用、感到受挫或感到无聊，我们应该为此烦恼吗？”

sentences.en: Wolpert’s response to the question about machine intelligence outstripping human intelligence was this: ‘In a limited sense it already has.
sentences.zh: 对于机器智能是否会超过人类智能，沃尔珀特这样回答：“从有限的意义上说，机器智能已经超过了人类智能。

sentences.en: Machines can already navigate, remember and search for items with an ability that far outstrips humans.
sentences.zh: 机器现在已经能导航、记忆和搜索物品，并且在这几方面的能力远超人类。

sentences.en: However, there is no machine that can identify visual objects or speech with the reliability and flexibility of humans. … Expecting a machine close to the creative intelligence of a human within the next 50 years would be highly ambitious.’
sentences.zh: 不过，在识别视觉对象或话语时，还没有哪种机器能达到人类那样的可靠性和灵活性。……指望未来五十年内出现一台创造性智能接近人类的机器，这个目标未免过于宏大。”

sentences.en: Richardson believes that our fear of machines becoming too advanced has more to do with human nature than anything intrinsic to the machines themselves.
sentences.zh: 理查森认为，我们害怕机器变得过于先进，这份恐惧更多地源于人性，而非机器本身的任何内在特质。

sentences.en: In her view, it stems from humans’ tendency to personify inanimate objects: we create machines based on representations of ourselves, imagine that machines think and behave as we do, and therefore see them as an autonomous threat.
sentences.zh: 在她看来，这种恐惧源于人把无生命物体人格化的倾向：我们按照自己的形象制造机器，想象机器像我们一样思考和行动，因而把机器视为一种能够自主行动的威胁。

sentences.en: ‘One of the consequences of thinking that the problem lies with machines is that … we tend to imagine they are greater and more powerful than they really are and subsequently they become so.’
sentences.zh: “认为问题出在机器身上，会带来一种后果：……我们往往把它们想象得比实际更了不起、更强大，而后来它们也真变得那么强了。”

sentences.en: This led on to the third question, ‘Should we be scared by advances in artificial intelligence?’
sentences.zh: 由此引出了第三个问题：“人工智能的进步应当让我们害怕吗？”

sentences.en: To this question, Rees replied, ‘Those who should be worried are the futurologists who believe in the so-called “singularity”.** … And another worry is that we are increasingly dependent on computer networks, and that these could behave like a single “brain” with a mind of its own, and with goals that may be contrary to human welfare.
sentences.zh: 里斯回答道：“该担心的是那些相信所谓‘奇点’的未来学家。……另一个令人担忧的问题是，我们越来越依赖计算机网络，而这些网络可能会像一个有自己想法的‘大脑’那样行事，追求的目标也可能与人类福祉背道而驰。

sentences.en: I think we should ensure that robots remain as no more than “idiot savants” lacking the capacity to outwit us, even though they may greatly surpass us in the ability to calculate and process information.’
sentences.zh: 我想，我们应该确保机器人充其量只是‘白痴天才’，没有本事用智谋胜过我们，即使它们在计算和处理信息方面可能远胜于我们。”

sentences.en: Wolpert’s response was to say that we have already seen the damaging effects of artificial intelligence in the form of computer viruses.
sentences.zh: 沃尔珀特回答说，我们已经从计算机病毒看到了人工智能的破坏性影响。

sentences.en: ‘But in this case,’ he says, ‘the real intelligence is the malicious designer.
sentences.zh: “但在这种情况下，”他说，“真正具有智能的是那个怀着恶意的设计者。

sentences.en: Critically, the benefits of computers outweigh the damage that computer viruses cause.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，计算机带来的益处超过了计算机病毒造成的损害。

sentences.en: Similarly, while there may be misuses of robotics in the near future, the benefits that they will bring are likely to outweigh these negative aspects.’
sentences.zh: 同样，虽然近期可能会出现滥用机器人技术的情况，但它带来的益处很可能超过这些不利影响。”

sentences.en: Richardson’s response to this question was this: ‘We need to ask why fears of artificial intelligence and robots persist; none have in fact risen up and challenged human supremacy.’
sentences.zh: 理查森这样回答：“我们需要问问自己，为什么对人工智能和机器人的恐惧会持续存在？事实上，至今没有一个机器人奋起挑战人类的主导地位。”

sentences.en: She believes that as robots have never shown themselves to be a threat to humans, it seems unlikely that they ever will.
sentences.zh: 她认为，既然机器人从未表现出对人类有威胁，今后它们似乎也不太可能成为威胁。

sentences.en: In fact, she went on, ‘Not all fear [robots]; many people welcome machine intelligence.’
sentences.zh: 她接着说，事实上，“并非所有人都害怕［机器人］，许多人欢迎机器智能。”

sentences.en: In answer to the fourth question, ‘What can science fiction tell us about robotics?’, Rees replied, ‘I sometimes advise students that it’s better to read first-rate science fiction than second-rate science – more stimulating, and perhaps no more likely to be wrong.’
sentences.zh: 第四个问题是“科幻作品能让我们对机器人技术有什么认识？”里斯回答：“我有时告诉学生，读一流的科幻作品比读二流的科学作品更好，前者更能启发思考，出错的可能性也未必就更大。”

sentences.en: As his response, Wolpert commented, ‘Science fiction has often been remarkable at predicting the future. … Science fiction has painted a vivid spectrum of possible futures, from cute and helpful robots to dystopian robotic societies.
sentences.zh: 沃尔珀特回答：“科幻作品在预测未来方面往往表现出色。……科幻作品生动地描绘出一系列可能的未来，既有可爱又乐于助人的机器人，也有反乌托邦式的机器人社会。

sentences.en: Interestingly, almost no science fiction envisages a future without robots.’
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，几乎没有科幻作品设想过一个没有机器人的未来。”

sentences.en: Finally, on the question of science fiction, Richardson pointed out that in modern society, people tend to think there is reality on the one hand, and fiction and fantasy on the other.
sentences.zh: 最后，谈到科幻作品，理查森指出，在现代社会，人们倾向于把现实归在一边，把虚构和幻想归在另一边。

sentences.en: She then explained that the division did not always exist, and that scientists and technologists made this separation because they wanted to carve out the sphere of their work.
sentences.zh: 她接着解释，这种区分并非一直都有。科学家和技术专家为了划定自己的工作领域，才作了这样的区分。

sentences.en: ‘But the divide is not so clear cut, and that is why the worlds seem to collide at times,’ she said.
sentences.zh: 她说：“但界限并没有这么分明，所以这两个世界有时似乎会碰撞在一起。”

sentences.en: ‘In some cases, we need to bring these different understandings together to get a whole perspective.
sentences.zh: “在一些情况下，我们需要把这些不同的理解结合起来，才能形成完整的认识。

sentences.en: Perhaps then, we won’t be so frightened that something we create as a copy of ourselves will be a [threat] to us.’
sentences.zh: 也许到了那时，我们就不会如此害怕自己按人类模样造出来的东西会对我们构成［威胁］。”
